findings.businessImpact: Unquantified. Conflicting canonical hints can make the preferred URL for the services page ambiguous to search engines, and a rendered hint pointing at the booking page could consolidate signals away from /services. No indexing, ranking, traffic, lead or booking effect is established: no Search Console, URL Inspection, GA4 or Bing evidence was supplied.
findings.description: Observed in the supplied synthetic capture (capturedAt 2026-11-19T11:30:00Z, inside the 2026-11-19T11:00:00Z–12:00:00Z window and within the 3600-second max age): the source-head layer (complete) declares canonical https://atlas.example/services, the rendered-head layer (complete) declares https://atlas.example/booking, and the HTTP Link layer (complete) declares no canonical. The evaluator returned canonical-consistency = fail (conflicting-declared-targets). Both declared targets are well-formed absolute URLs without fragments (canonical-target-format = pass). Which target the owner intends is not supplied, so owner intent remains unknown, and the cause of the change between source and rendered head (for example client-side head rewriting) is not established by this evidence.
findings.recommendation: After the SEO owner states the preferred canonical for https://atlas.example/services, website engineering should make the source head, rendered head and (if used) HTTP Link header declare that single target for the mobile/anonymous state, and identify what changes the rendered canonical to /booking. This report does not choose the correct target and does not authorize any website change.
findings.title: Source and rendered canonical declarations conflict on /services (mobile, anonymous)
findings.verification: Supply a fresh canonical-capture-v1 export for the same URL, environment, mobile profile and anonymous state with all three layers complete; rerun enterprise-technical-seo-evaluate with the owner's expectedCanonical and confirm canonical-consistency and canonical-owner-intent both pass; then supply a scoped URL Inspection export to check the provider-selected canonical.

methodology: Coverage concerns declared checks, not every possible website defect.
Historical measurements are retained separately from current observations.
Structural validation and attributed review do not independently authenticate provider data.
No raw evidence payloads are included; inspect the source run using its recorded digest.
Redaction requires review; pattern matching is not a guarantee that every confidential value was identified.

narrative.text: Scope: one synthetic URL (https://atlas.example/services), environment synthetic, mobile profile, anonymous state, observation window 2026-11-19T11:00:00Z (inclusive) to 12:00:00Z (exclusive), assessed at 2026-11-19T12:00:00Z for the lead-generation and booking profiles. Inventory mode is sample and discovery is not complete; no page content, HTML or rendered DOM was supplied, so no content inventory was created and the content quality, SEO-content, AI search optimization (AIO, not the Google product AI Overviews), answer-quality (AEO) and generative-visibility (GEO) dimensions were not assessed.

Observed (supplied capture, 11:30:00Z, fresh until 12:30:00Z): source head declares https://atlas.example/services; rendered head declares https://atlas.example/booking; HTTP Link declares none; all three layers are marked complete. Result: canonical-target-format pass, canonical-consistency fail.

The services page sends different canonical hints before and after rendering. Because owner intent was not supplied, this report treats the conflict itself as the defect and does not state which URL should be canonical or why the rendered head changes.

Recorded separately: collection attempt attempt-one (11:35:00Z–11:36:00Z, synthetic) returned status unknown with gap browser-unavailable and no capture. The capture-availability check for target services-canonical-capture stays unknown (capture-unavailable). The failure does not alter or invalidate the earlier supplied capture, and it is not evidence of a site defect.

Unavailable evidence, kept unknown (not pass, not zero): owner canonical policy, URL Inspection / provider index state and Google-selected canonical, GA4, Google Search Console, Bing, GTM, consent policy, performance field/lab, accessibility, and runtime indexability. Neither supplied export authenticates production behaviour; hash checks establish integrity only.

Priority order: (1) SEO owner supplies the canonical policy for /services; (2) engineering traces the rendered-head rewrite to /booking; (3) recapture all three layers and re-evaluate in a new run; (4) supply URL Inspection. Outstanding owner requests and export instructions are listed in the data request section.
